query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: If you are in the 0, 10, or 15% tax bracket, it is likely you would benefit from contributing to your company's Roth 401k.
supporting_text: At these income levels, it is likely that your income will grow over time and you will be in a higher tax bracket at some point in the future. There is also the potential that these very low tax rates increase in the future, so taking advantage of paying taxes on these funds now at a very low rate, allowing the funds to grow tax free, and making tax free withdrawals in retirement is likely a good bet.
caveats: Future income may rise, affecting tax bracket
Tax rates may increase in the future

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: If you are in the 25% tax bracket or higher, a closer analysis of tax benefits is needed before deciding.
supporting_text: At these tax rates, you want to do a closer analysis of what other tax benefits you might be missing out on by pulling that money into taxation now. For example, the capital gains tax rate for taxpayers in the 0, 10, and 15% brackets is 0%.
conditions: Current tax bracket is 25% or higher
caveats: Higher income earners may benefit more from traditional pre-tax 401k contributions

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: If you are just getting started in your career and expect your income to grow, this is likely the time to take advantage of the Roth 401k option.
supporting_text: The earlier you can get started making contributions, the longer those funds have to grow tax free. When your income rises, you can split your contributions between traditional and Roth, adjusting more to traditional for the tax benefit as your income rises.
conditions: Early in career with expected income growth
caveats: Life changes may affect income and contribution strategy

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: Contributing to a Roth IRA is beneficial as it allows for tax-free growth and withdrawals.
supporting_text: The Roth IRA is the gold standard of retirement savings accounts. Contributions go in after-tax, earnings grow tax free, and withdrawals are completely tax free in retirement.
conditions: Adjusted Gross Income is below phase out ranges
caveats: Full contributions are limited by income
Income above phase out ranges may still allow for Roth IRA access through other means

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: It's important to make the Roth/Traditional 401k decision in the context of your overall financial plan.
supporting_text: Retirement is of course not the only goal you are saving for. Saving in your 401k is great and we encourage our clients to max out their contributions to the best of their ability.
conditions: Considering overall financial goals and needs
caveats: Competing financial goals may affect retirement savings strategy

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: If you're in a low tax bracket now and expect to be in a higher bracket later, you may want to consider a Roth.
supporting_text: A Roth account doesn't reduce your taxes today; but in retirement, when you need it, qualified distributions are tax-free. Roth IRAs are best for lower earning years, or if your tax rate will remain the same or increase in retirement.
conditions: Currently in a low tax bracket
Expect to be in a higher tax bracket later
caveats: Tax rates are hard to predict due to changes in the law
Uncertainty around future income levels

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: A traditional IRA may be better if you're in your peak earning years or expect to have lower taxable income in retirement.
supporting_text: With a traditional IRA, you pay less in taxes every year that you contribute. But generally, you'll have to pay taxes on the money you withdraw in retirement.
conditions: Expect lower taxable income in retirement
caveats: May not be suitable for everyone
Depends on individual financial situations

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: Roth accounts generally are better for heirs, since assets usually will be withdrawn tax-free.
supporting_text: If, like many people, you have more assets in traditional accounts than in Roth accounts, adding to your Roth assets improves tax diversification. This hedges against the risk of changes in tax laws or your personal circumstances.
conditions: Have more assets in traditional accounts
Concerned about tax implications for heirs
caveats: Roth accounts may not be flexible for all assets
Consideration of individual circumstances is necessary

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: If you're struggling to save, the traditional pretax approach may enable you to get your employer's full 401(k) match with less impact on your take-home pay.
supporting_text: This is because taxable income is reduced by the amount of your contribution. Having trouble deciding? If you're still unsure of what to do in your situation, the tiebreaker often should be in the Roth account's favor.

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: Contributing to a Roth IRA allows for tax-free withdrawals in retirement.
supporting_text: A Roth IRA allows you to contribute after-tax dollars. The money in your Roth IRA grows through annual contributions and investment appreciation, with annual contributions limited to $6,500 a year ($7,500 if you're over age 50). Contributions and potential investment gains accumulate tax-free.
conditions: You must earn income below a certain level ($153,000 for single tax filers, or less than $228,000 for those married and filing jointly).
caveats: The Roth IRA doesn't offer any current-year tax benefits.
Investments held in a Roth IRA usually don't guarantee performance, so your investments could fluctuate in value.

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: Contributing to a traditional 401(k) can provide immediate tax benefits.
supporting_text: A traditional 401(k) is funded with pre-tax dollars, which means you won't pay taxes on it until you begin taking withdrawals. Your contributions may also be tax-deductible, helping give you immediate tax benefits.
conditions: You can begin withdrawing from your 401(k) at age 59½, or if you meet other criteria dictated by the IRS.
caveats: Withdrawals from a traditional 401(k) will be taxed as ordinary income.
The value of your 401(k) may fluctuate based on investment earnings.

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: Residents and military members should maximize Roth contributions.
supporting_text: If you're a resident or military member, maximize Roth contributions. This is because they are likely in lower income years and can benefit from tax-free growth.

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: If you save and invest more than 20% of your gross income, lean more toward Roth investments.
supporting_text: If you save and invest more than 20% of your gross income, lean a little more toward Roth investments. This is because you may benefit from tax-free growth on a larger amount.
caveats: If you save and invest less, use tax-deferred accounts preferentially.

query: Should I contribute to a Roth IRA or a traditional 401k?
main_claim: You can do Roth conversions in later years when your income may be lower.
supporting_text: One of the best arguments against pre-paying your taxes by making Roth 401(k) contributions is that you don't know what the future holds. You can do Roth conversions in later years when your income may be lower.
